title: A Semester for the Locker
premise: Edmund Nakamura, a senior who bakes her emotions into bread and counts the days to graduation, is paired for a semester project with her nemesis, popular student-council president Priya Okafor. Their assignment—documenting the school's history—leads them to a sealed locker containing records of a decades-old cover-up: a student's death the school board erased from memory. As Edmund and Priya move from enemies to uneasy allies to something like friends, they must decide whether exposing the truth is worth sacrificing Edmund's safe invisibility and Priya's polished future. The book ends at graduation, where Edmund reads the buried student's name aloud during her valedictory-adjacent speech, forcing the board's resignation and finally claiming her own place in the school's story.
about_author: Oscar Fairweather is a former high school debate coach who spent ten years watching teenagers discover that silence is a choice, not a personality. He writes in a converted garage above a bakery, insisting the smell of yeast improves his prose.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet her at 4 a.m. in her family bakery, kneading anxiety into sourdough, counting down 178 days to graduation. She narrates her strategy of total social invisibility. Emotional beat: weary resignation disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Ms. Adeyemi announces the semester-long 'Living History' project and pairs Edmund with Priya Okafor, who once humiliated her freshman year. Edmund's POV; panic rises like overproofed dough. Beat: dread and the collapse of her survival plan.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: First working session in the library. Priya proposes a glossy timeline of school achievements; Edmund silently resists. Alternating POV establishes their mutual contempt and hidden insecurities. Beat: cold truce, sparks of friction.

chapters.title: Bread for Enemies
chapters.summary: Edmund accidentally leaves a loaf of 'grudge bread'—dense, bitter rye—in her locker; Priya finds it and, shockingly, likes it. They negotiate project terms over crumbs. Beat: grudging curiosity, first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Researching yearbooks in the archive, they find a gap: no photos or records from 1987, and a padlocked locker welded shut in the east hallway. Priya's POV; her council-president polish slips as she admits she's noticed the gap too. Beat: shared intrigue.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Didn't Say
chapters.summary: They interview retired custodian Mr. Hollis, who goes pale at the mention of Locker 114 and mutters a name—'Marisol'—before shutting his door. Edmund's POV. Beat: first real fear; the project stops being homework.

chapters.title: Rising Tension
chapters.summary: Priya discovers her faculty advisor has quietly removed their archive access request. Someone upstairs is watching. Alternating POV; they argue about whether to stop. Beat: paranoia, and the choice to continue binding them together.

chapters.title: Marisol Vega
chapters.summary: Through microfilm at the county library, they learn Marisol Vega died on campus in 1987—an accident the papers called one thing and a single surviving classmate calls another. Priya's POV. Beat: grief for a stranger, moral weight settling in.

chapters.title: The Board's Quiet Hands
chapters.summary: Edmund tails a school board member to a diner meeting and overhears talk of 'the Vega settlement.' She panics and bakes all night. Beat: terror transformed into resolve; invisibility starts feeling like complicity.

chapters.title: Allies and Liars
chapters.summary: They recruit two friends—a hacker-ish yearbook editor and Marisol's grandniece, a sophomore—to help. Priya risks her college recommendation letters by signing her name to records requests. Beat: belonging, chosen deliberately for the first time.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: The principal summons them separately, offering Edmund a scholarship letter and Priya a warning about 'distraction.' Each refuses, then compares notes. Beat: temptation refused; trust cemented under pressure.

chapters.title: Sourdough and Secrets
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter: Edmund teaches Priya to bake; Priya reveals her immigrant parents' sacrifices riding on her perfect record. Marisol's grandniece shares family letters hinting Marisol was bullied by students whose names are now on the school's donor wall. Beat: intimacy and deepening stakes.

chapters.title: Vandalism
chapters.summary: Someone trashes the bakery overnight—flour everywhere, ovens damaged. The message is clear. Edmund's family absorbs the loss without asking why. Beat: rage and guilt; Edmund realizes her secrecy endangered everyone she loves.

chapters.title: Confession at the Wall
chapters.summary: Mr. Hollis, moved by the vandalism, confesses he was ordered to weld Locker 114 shut in 1987 and hands over the key he was supposed to destroy. Beat: an old man's shame becomes their inheritance.

chapters.title: Inside Locker 114
chapters.summary: They open the locker: Marisol's journal, a broken locket, and board minutes documenting a hazing death recast as an accident, signed by men whose names still appear on buildings. Beat: awe, horror, and the terrible clarity of proof.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Priya's mother finds copies of the documents and forbids her to continue weeks before early-decision deadlines. Priya wavers; Edmund accuses her of being exactly the kind of person who buries things. Beat: the alliance shatters at its weakest seam.

chapters.title: Alone with the Truth
chapters.summary: Edmund considers publishing alone but realizes the story needs Priya's credibility—and that her anger echoes the bullies who killed Marisol. She bakes reconciliation bread and waits outside Priya's house. Beat: humility; choosing people over pride.

chapters.title: The Deadline
chapters.summary: Reconciled, they plan to present everything at the semester showcase—the one night the whole town attends. The board moves to cancel the showcase. The students organize, going public online with the journal excerpts. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Showcase
chapters.summary: Climax part one: despite cancellation, students fill the gym anyway. Edmund and Priya present 'Living History' as Marisol's story, reading her journal aloud as donors and board members walk out. Beat: courage made communal; the room chooses to listen.

chapters.title: The Name Out Loud
chapters.summary: Climax part two: at graduation rehearsal-turned-rally, Edmund abandons her scripted speech and speaks Marisol Vega's name into the microphone. The board resigns within days; the district announces a memorial and scholarship. Beat: catharsis; invisibility abandoned forever.

chapters.title: Crumb and Crust
chapters.summary: Falling action: consequences ripple—Priya loses one recommendation but gains another from a journalist; Mr. Hollis attends the memorial; the bakery rebuilds. Edmund and Priya acknowledge what they've become to each other, unnamed but certain. Beat: tender aftermath.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Edmund's POV: she walks the stage not as a sentence served but as a person who belongs. Her last loaf of high school bread—light, sweet, honest—sits in Locker 114's replacement display case beside Marisol's photo. Beat: belonging earned, memory honored, future open.
